checks.name: refusal-is-not-weakened
checks.summary: A9, refusal asserted rather than promised, in the same change that makes a real cursor work. New test TestTheBacklogStillRefusesACursorItDidNotIssue in internal/api/api_test.go. VERDICT: `--- PASS` for the parent and for all seven subtests, `ok github.com/takushi/agentic-loop-foundation/v2/internal/api 0.005s`, and PASS again under `make component-api` and under the -race validation run. REFUSED WITH 400 AND "error":"invalid_request", each asserted: (1) a fabricated cursor that is not base64url (fabricated.cursor*not-base64url); (2) a well-formed base64url envelope whose version is not v1 ({"v":"v2",...}); (3) a truncated prefix of a cursor the route ACTUALLY issued in the same test (the first half of the real next_cursor; prefixes of length 20, 21, 22, 23 and 44 were all measured 400 before the assertion was written); (4) another collection's key space -- the Firestore DOCUMENT KEY of an Increment, base64url("increment-b"), which decodes cleanly and is not a cursor envelope; and additionally (5) another paged read's own cursor shape, base64url of "<expires-at>\n<document-key>" as ExpiredActiveLeases emits it. The test also asserts the cursor the route itself issued is accepted with 200, so the file cannot pass by refusing everything. MEASURED DISAGREEMENT WITH THE WORK ORDER'S PARENTHETICAL, recorded rather than acted on, because acting on it is exactly what the design forbids: A9 names the fourth shape as 'a well-formed v1 envelope whose after names another collection's key space (an Increment id)'. Measured on this tree, base64url({"v":"v1","after":"increment-b"}) returns 200, not 400 -- and it must, because A9's own boundary clause says a well-formed envelope naming a Requirement id that does not exist is not an error today and must not become one, and an Increment id is precisely such a string: nothing structurally distinguishes the two id namespaces inside the envelope, application.decodeCursor validates shape and not existence, and PathKey accepts any non-empty valid-UTF-8 key under the byte limit. Turning that shape into a 400 would be a behaviour change turning a currently-accepted cursor into a refusal, which the constraints forbid outright. So the fourth shape is asserted in the form that IS refused -- another collection's document key space -- and the two accepted shapes are pinned as 200 in the same test (v1-envelope-naming-a-requirement-that-does-not-exist and v1-envelope-naming-another-aggregates-id) so a later change cannot quietly turn either into a 400. THE BOUNDARY THIS TEST MUST NOT CROSS, stated as A9 requires: a well-formed envelope naming a Requirement id that does not exist is NOT an error; measured, a fabricated document id returns an empty page from Firestore (0 rows, no error) and the memory adapter returns the page positioned after that key. Nothing in this task's diff touches application.decodeCursor, PathKey, boundPageSize, application.MaxPageSize or internal/api's error classification, so no refusal was weakened and none was added.
